clue.text: Bolted many together?

blocks.note: surface reading: fastened lots of things with nuts and bolts
setter's reading: ran off in panic, as a herd does all at once

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bolted' looks like fixing with bolts; it is fleeing, and the 'many together' is a whole herd charging off as one.
explanation.definitionFit: A herd that rushes off in sudden panic as one mass is said to have done this, past tense of the verb.

clue.text: Copies sent up, including one in colour

indicators.note: in a down clue, sent up means read from bottom to top
including something means taking it inside

blocks.note: to ape someone is to copy them

explanation.surface: Duplicates are posted off, including one printed in colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A reddish-brown tint, originally from cuttlefish ink and familiar from old photographs, is a named colour.

clue.text: People's leader, such as Lincoln

blocks.note: first meaning: the patriarch who led the Hebrew people
second meaning: a first name borne by the sixteenth US president

explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln makes 'people's leader' sound like a president of the people; the first meaning is the Biblical patriarch.
explanation.definitionFit: The Biblical patriarch is the father of the Israelite nation, and Lincoln's given name was the same.

clue.text: Simple difference of opinion, but he goes to court

explanation.surface: A small disagreement ends up in a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: The party who brings a case against another in a civil lawsuit is the one taking the matter before a judge.

clue.text: Honour saint at home, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it

blocks.note: to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: A holy person is honoured at home with a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: An award or mark of special merit, as in graduating with first-class standing, is an honour.

clue.text: Note in sound money

indicators.note: sound tells us we want how a word is spoken rather than spelt

explanation.surface: A banknote, printed in solid currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' and 'sound money' suggest banknotes and solid currency; the note is musical.
explanation.definitionFit: In tonic sol-fa the first degree of the scale is a musical tone named with this syllable.

clue.text: Blame one laid on head of Dean Swift

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: to take the rap is to take the blame

explanation.surface: Jonathan Swift, Dean of St Patrick's, is censured for some misdeed.
explanation.walkthrough: Dean Swift reads as the satirist Jonathan Swift, who was Dean of St Patrick's in Dublin; here Swift is the plain adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something moving at great speed, so they are straightforward synonyms.

clue.text: Condition under which a horse races

blocks.note: first meaning: a clause added to a document or agreement
second meaning: the jockey on its back, literally above the horse

explanation.walkthrough: 'Condition under which' reads as one phrase about racing terms; split it, and the second half is the person a horse runs beneath.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra clause added to a contract is called this, and so is the jockey sitting astride a horse.

clue.text: Weak case made for charitable collection

explanation.surface: A flimsy argument is put forward for a church fund.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weak case' sounds like a feeble argument; it is a container.
explanation.definitionFit: A slotted container in a church receives alms gifted to help needy people, so it holds a charitable collection.

clue.text: Dealt out two of diamonds and two of spades - needs shuffle

indicators.note: two of a word here means its opening pair of letters
shuffling cards mixes their order, so these letters are mixed too

explanation.surface: A card player dealt the two of diamonds and two of spades, then wants to reshuffle.
explanation.walkthrough: The card-game surface hides two letters from each suit name.
explanation.definitionFit: To distribute or hand out portions, as a pharmacist or a dealer does, is a plain synonym.

clue.text: Has prep to revise, maybe

indicators.note: revising reworks material into a new form, so these letters get rearranged

explanation.surface: A pupil possibly has homework to go over.
explanation.walkthrough: Prep is British school slang for homework.
explanation.definitionFit: Both adverbs express possibility without certainty, a straightforward synonym pair.

clue.text: Pelt American all round the ring - - that's sickening

indicators.note: going all round something means enclosing it on every side

blocks.note: a ring is shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone hurls an American fur all around a boxing ring, which is disgusting.
explanation.walkthrough: The pelt and the American together go all round the ring, so the O sits between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something so ugly or repellent it turns the stomach; the two adjectives are close synonyms.

clue.text: He splits a couple of poles made of wood

indicators.note: something that splits a thing goes into it, breaking it apart

blocks.note: S and N, the south and north poles

explanation.surface: A man cleaves a pair of wooden posts.
explanation.walkthrough: HE goes between S and N, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things fashioned from the timber of the ash tree, so it fits 'made of wood'.

clue.text: Having no remedy, suffer before getting island retreat

indicators.note: retreating means going back, so the island's name is read the other way

blocks.note: to incur a loss is to suffer it

explanation.surface: An ailment without cure has to be endured before a holiday on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Elba, Napoleon's first place of exile, is the crossword's favourite island.
explanation.definitionFit: A disease beyond any cure is one for which no treatment exists, so the phrase is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Agreed about a spiteful woman being involved

indicators.note: going about something means wrapping around it

blocks.note: a cat is a catty, malicious woman

explanation.surface: Someone consented to a spiteful woman being brought into things.
explanation.definitionFit: An involved plot or argument is intricate and hard to follow, so the adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Margaret turned to stone

indicators.note: turned around means facing the other way, so the name is read backwards

explanation.surface: Margaret was petrified, like a figure in myth.
explanation.definitionFit: A precious stone, cut and polished for jewellery, is called by this short word.

clue.text: Ring-fighter is happy to, in the fresh air

indicators.note: being in something means placed inside it
a fresh version is newly made, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A boxer is content to be out of doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring-fighter' suggests a boxer; the ring is the Roman arena.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman combatant fought in the arena, an enclosed ring, for public entertainment, so he is a ring-fighter.

clue.text: Exact monies may be needed for these

definitions.text: Exact monies may be needed for these

indicators.note: the letters must be worked into what is needed, so they are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: The precise sums of money are required to settle certain bills.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the anagram and a description of the answer: the Revenue wants exact sums for INCOME TAXES.
explanation.definitionFit: Levies charged by the state on earnings must be paid to the penny, which the whole sentence describes.

clue.text: She might well make man target

definitions.text: She might well make man target

indicators.note: to make something is to form it, so these letters are formed into a new word

explanation.surface: A fierce woman could easily turn a man into her victim.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the answer and contains its letters: a scold would make a man her target.
explanation.definitionFit: A termagant is a harsh, overbearing, quarrelsome woman, who might well pick on a husband.

clue.text: Dictator hated for ill-treatment

indicators.note: ill-treatment means the words are knocked about, so their letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written, borrowed from ill-treatment

explanation.surface: A tyrant is loathed for his cruelty to people.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is also a fair description of the man, and 'ill' does double duty as part of the signal word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nazi leader ruled Germany as an absolute autocrat, so he is a famous example of the class.

clue.text: More than one player is in new boots

indicators.note: being in something means placed inside it
a new version of a word has its letters set out afresh

explanation.surface: Several footballers are wearing new boots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Player' and 'boots' suggest football; the players are musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of an orchestra who play the double-reed woodwind are plural musicians, so more than one player.

clue.text: Not happy with some gratuitous advice

indicators.note: some of the words means only part of them is used, a run of letters inside

blocks.note: the end of one word and start of the next

explanation.surface: Someone is unhappy about receiving unsolicited advice.
explanation.definitionFit: Unhappy and sorrowful are near synonyms, so 'not happy' is a plain dictionary equivalent.

clue.text: Elegant French female

blocks.note: setter's reading: the feminine form of a French adjective meaning well groomed

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a description of a stylish Parisienne; it is the French word for elegant, in its feminine spelling with the extra E.
explanation.definitionFit: Borrowed into English, this French adjective means well groomed and sophisticated, used of a woman in its feminine form.

clue.text: In love and caring fantastically - it's a sort of chemistry

definitions.note: adjective naming a branch of chemistry

indicators.note: something done fantastically is wild and fanciful, so the word's letters are scrambled

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: Being in love and wildly affectionate is a kind of chemistry between people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chemistry' suggests romantic attraction, matching 'in love'; it is the science.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the main branches of chemistry studies compounds that are not carbon-based, and carries this name.

clue.text: Traveller has a lot of discomfort on yacht

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so this part comes first

blocks.note: to give someone gyp is to cause them pain

explanation.surface: A wanderer suffers badly from seasickness aboard a yacht.
explanation.walkthrough: Gyp is British slang for pain or trouble; SY marks a steam yacht.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Romany people, traditionally nomadic, is often called a traveller.

clue.text: In principle, ring after eleven in the morning

indicators.note: coming after places the ring at the end of the number
being in something means sitting inside it, enclosed

blocks.note: the Roman numeral, also a cricket or football team

explanation.surface: In theory, a phone call comes after eleven o'clock in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring after eleven' sounds like a phone call at 11am; the ring is the letter-shaped one and follows the Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-evident truth taken as a starting point for reasoning is a basic principle, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Lady in Mother's Union

blocks.note: joining a second mother: a dam is an animal mother

explanation.surface: A woman belongs to the Mothers' Union church organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Mother's Union' as a joining of two words for mother: MA and DAM, a dam being an animal's mother. The Mothers' Union is an Anglican women's charity.
explanation.definitionFit: Madam is a polite form of address for a woman, used as 'my lady' once was.

clue.text: One drunk turns to espy another

indicators.note: turning round means facing the other way, so the drunkard's short name is read backwards

blocks.note: to spot something is to catch sight of it

explanation.surface: A drunkard swivels round to catch sight of a fellow boozer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One drunk' looks like the definition; it is the wordplay, and 'another' is the definition, meaning a second drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A tosspot is an old word for a heavy drinker, so it is indeed another of the same kind.

clue.text: Queen's consort

blocks.note: surface reading: the husband of a reigning monarch
setter's reading: a female cat, whose mate is a male cat

explanation.walkthrough: It looks like the royal Prince Consort; a queen is a female cat, and her mate is the male.
explanation.definitionFit: A breeding female cat is called a queen, and the male that pairs with her goes by this name.

clue.text: In entering new trade, one should be

definitions.note: one should be trained, completing the sentence

indicators.note: entering something means going inside it
a new version of a word is a remade one, its letters arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Anyone joining a new line of work ought to receive instruction.
explanation.walkthrough: The sentence is completed by the answer: on entering a new trade, one should be TRAINED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone taught the skills of a job has been instructed, which is what a newcomer to a craft ought to be.

clue.text: For hazardous runs. I hit ball in air

blocks.note: to sky a ball is to hit it high into the air

explanation.surface: A batsman explains a dangerous shot: running, then lofting the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, to sky the ball is to hit it straight up, risking a catch.
explanation.definitionFit: Both adjectives describe something full of danger or chance of loss, a plain synonym pair.

clue.text: The farthest one can get from a bank

definitions.text: The farthest one can get from a bank

blocks.clueFragment: The farthest one can get from a bank
blocks.note: surface reading: as far as possible from a financial institution
setter's reading: the edge of a river, so the point furthest from it is out in the flow's centre

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' suggests money; it is a riverbank, and the farthest point from either side is out in the very centre of the current.
explanation.definitionFit: The middle of a river's flow is equidistant from both shores, the point most remote from either edge.
